newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq Israel asks court to halt strike.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq Israel asks court to halt strike.

text.p: A Bezeq Israel Telecom spokesman said the company will file a motion in court on Wednesday afternoon to halt a three-day-old strike by its workers, while the Histadrut labour federation warned of brief sympathy stoppages at government-owned companies.

Bezeq workers walked out to protest the government's failure to inform them in advance of an agreement on Monday to sell 12.5 percent of Bezeq's shares to Merrill Lynch for $250 million, officials at the workers' union said.
Merrill Lynch plans to sell the shares to its clients.

The workers said Communications Minister Limor Livnat had promised the government would not sell any shares in Bezeq without first discussing it with the workers, who fear the privatisation of the company will lead to massive layoffs.
The Bezeq spokesman said the workers should not be striking since their grievance was with the government, not the company.

Shlomo Shani, chairman of the Histadrut's trade union department, warned of disruption at government owned companies on Wednesday afternoon as a result of planned work stoppages in sympathy with Bezeq's union.

He said workers at Israel's Airports Authority, El Al Israel Airlines, Israel Aircraft Industries, Israel Military Industries, Israel Electric Corp and the Mekoroth water authority would stop work for one to two hours while the court hears Bezeq's motion.
Flights at Ben Gurion Airport will be delayed as a result, Shani said.
Any further labour action will depend on the court's decision, he added.
